slides.1.title: Oregon: Pinot Noir and labelling
slides.1.highlights.0.title: 2022 plantings
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Total 44,487 acres; Pinot Noir 24,729, Pinot Gris 5,546, Chardonnay 2,518, Syrah 1,679, Cabernet Sauvignon 1,557
slides.1.highlights.1.title: 90% and 75%
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Oregon generally requires at least 90% of the named variety; Bordeaux and Rhône varieties, Sangiovese, Tempranillo, Zinfandel and Tannat follow the federal 75% standard
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Place names
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Place names on labels must be official appellations
slides.1.content: Oregon is stricter than federal rules: Pinot Noir must reach 90%.
slides.2.title: Washington: reds and whites
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Main grapes
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cabernet Sauvignon, Riesling, Chardonnay, Merlot and Syrah
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The giant
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Chateau Ste. Michelle is the largest producer, owning more than a third of the state's vineyard land, and was named Best American Winery in 1988
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Scale
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Over 940 wineries and over 55,000 acres of vineyards in 2017
slides.2.content: Washington has both large-scale producers and boutique wineries.
slides.3.title: New York: Riesling, ice wine and sparkling
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Riesling
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The Finger Lakes' signature, from dry to sweet, with acidity kept by the cool climate
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Ice wine
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Grapes freeze naturally on the vine and are pressed frozen, giving a little concentrated, sugar-rich juice; it needs cold enough winters
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Sparkling
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Cool-climate acidity suits sparkling base wine; both Oregon and New York make traditional-method sparkling
slides.3.content: Cool climate = high acidity = a natural edge for Riesling, ice wine and sparkling.
